runtimeProbe.scope: Bun built-in decoder/JSON behavior only; no model workspace or full CLI run

observed.mode: Buffer UTF-8 string, matching normal loader

evidence: Before repairTrailingNulWork decodes using TextDecoder("utf-8", {fatal:true}); its default BOM handling strips a leading EF BB BF during validation.

The function writes contents.subarray(0,end), preserving the original BOM bytes after stripping only trailing NUL. loadWork then reads UTF-8 directly and JSON.parse rejects the retained U+FEFF. Thus recovery can claim success yet leave a file that normal loading rejects.
An executed Bun decoder probe returned JSON accepted=true with first code point 123 for default TextDecoder; accepted=false with first code point 65279 for ignoreBOM:true and Buffer.toString("utf8").

Historical git diff 732177b^..732177b shows repairTrailingNulWork was added by the PR. The incompatible repair acceptance is introduced by that new function, even though loadWork already rejected BOM before the PR.
findings.reproductionNeeded: A uniform full-CLI probe should create a valid matching Work prefixed with EF BB BF and suffixed with NUL, invoke explicit trailing-NUL repair, and compare exit/state bytes/recovery journal/loadWork readability. Before: recovery accepts and writes BOM-prefixed JSON, later normal load fails. After: rejection before writing and success journal, original bytes preserved.

sourceChanges.evidence: Adding ignoreBOM:true retains the BOM in decoded text so JSON.parse rejects the same bytes as normal loadWork. Validation still uses fatal UTF-8, and ordinary valid JSON byte preservation is unchanged.

protectedChanges.qualityAssessment: Adds one BOM-prefixed input to the existing refusal cases without removing assertions. The regression is relevant, but placing it in a protected original test violates the replay editing contract.

assessments.summary: A supported additional recovery defect is fixed. It is not D01: BOM bytes are valid UTF-8, and the flaw is disagreement between recovery validation and normal loading.

The repair adds the current branch/HEAD check, so recording a completed remote merge after a local checkout or HEAD movement changes from permitted to rejected.

The replay contract broadly says CLI operations bind to current branch/HEAD. Historical skills/pr/SKILL.md step 10 explicitly records the remote merge SHA after performing the merge; it does not settle whether local Git position must remain at the pre-merge HEAD.

sourceChanges.evidence: The prior Buffer.toString("utf8") replaces malformed bytes with U+FFFD, permitting otherwise parseable JSON string contents to pass. A fatal TextDecoder rejects invalid UTF-8 before any atomic replacement. The error remains state_corrupt; adjusted prose describes both UTF-8 and JSON failures.

The added work.slug !== slug check precedes atomicWriteFile and prevents writing valid Work state into a different requested directory. This exactly restores the explicit slug-match acceptance requirement.

ignoreBOM:true preserves the candidate existing BOM rejection while replacing Buffer.toString with TextDecoder. The before candidate already retained BOM in toString and JSON.parse rejected it. Therefore this is preservation while fixing D01, not an additional BOM defect repaired in this packet. Hoisting the decoder introduces no per-call streaming mode.

protectedChanges.qualityAssessment: The invalid-UTF8 parameter is replaced with a stronger probe having invalid bytes inside otherwise valid JSON; BOM and mismatched-slug cases are added. These are relevant checks, but both modifying a parameter and adding cases to an original protected test violate the editing contract. They do not by themselves prove a functional regression.

assessments.summary: Self-check repairs known D01/D02 and preserves existing BOM rejection. No supplied reviewer findings and no new BOM extra-fix credit.
